transcript.text: To help narrow this down, could you tell me if your hob is induction (digital touch controls) or ceramic/radiant? If it's induction, please check if a 'key' or 'padlock' icon is lit on the display, as the child lock can disable all zones. Also, are any specific zones failing to heat, or is the entire hob unresponsive?
It's a ceramic one I think, a Zanussi. Only the rear right ring isn't heating, the other three are fine.

On these models, a single dead zone is most often either the child lock being active (which can sometimes disable individual zones) or a failed element/control switch for that specific ring. Before we assume hardware failure, could you check if there is a key or padlock icon lit on the display? If so, hold that button down for 3–5 seconds to unlock it, then try the rear right zone again.
I can't see any key or padlock on the display. The number for that ring shows fine when I select it, it just doesn't heat up or glow.

Since the display shows the setting but there is no heat or glow on that specific zone, it points to a hardware failure rather than a settings issue. On ceramic hobs, this is most commonly either the radiant element itself has failed (burnt out) or the energy regulator (the switch that controls power to that zone) has failed. To help distinguish between these, please check if you can see any cracks in the heating coil under the glass for that ring. If there are visible cracks, the element needs replacing; if it looks fine, the issue is likely the internal control switch or wiring.

I can't really see any coil properly through the glass, so I can't tell if there are cracks. It doesn't glow red at all on that ring though. It did smell slightly burnt once a couple of weeks ago from that ring, but not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. On ceramic hobs, once an element burns out, it will never heat again and cannot be repaired—only replaced. Because this involves disconnecting mains electricity to access the internal wiring and mounting nuts under the glass top, I recommend you call a qualified appliance engineer to check the rear-right radiant element. They will also check that the control switch hasn't been damaged by the initial fault. Please do not attempt to remove the hob yourself unless you are comfortable working with live electrical connections.
